title: 30-min pairing micro-debrief: Zoe Park (SWE II)
recommendation: advance to longer systems pairing (lean yes) — wants to see deep runtime tradeoffs and perf microbenchmarks
body:
Quick context: 30 minute pairing focusing on a small runtime problem: implement a simplified KV prefix cache with eviction and hot-prefix fast-path. Goal was to watch thought process, incremental testing, and low-level tradeoffs. This is a personal micro-debrief — raw notes, typos, and open questions below.

Summary impressions:
- Strong low-level instincts. Reached viable approach quickly (sharded cache + ring buffer for hot entries).
- Comfortable with Rust but also pragmatic about iterating in Go/Python for perf experiments. Mentioned prior work shipping a lock-free ring buffer in Rust at scale.
- Good tradeoff language: memory vs latency, cold-starts vs steady-state, per-tenant isolation.
- Less polished on API ergonomics for multi-tenant rollout (we want explicit canary/rollback hooks integrated with control plane).

What they built during pairing (notes):
- Proposed shards keyed by prefix hash, sized by observed active prefixes; used an LRU-like eviction per shard.
- For hot-prefix fast path, sketched a small fixed-size ring buffer for recently used KV entries to serve common short-prefix lookups without touching the shard mutex.
- Wrote a tiny Rust prototype pseudo-code (we walked it through together). Tested mentally some race scenarios and suggested atomic pointer swap for single-producer single-consumer in the hot-path.
- Brought up potential phantom reads on rebalancing shards; suggested background reindexing with versioned pointers.

Strengths observed:
- Excellent at reasoning about memory layout and cache-line effects — specifically called out padding to avoid false sharing on A100 host threads (nice detail).
- Knows when to stop over-engineering: proposed a simple fallback to mutex-backed shard for rare long-tail prefixes.
- Good debugging heuristics: would add a perf counter for hot-path hit-rate, tail-latency percentiles, and a safety meter for outstanding KV growth.

Concerns / gaps:
- Rollout/ops specifics were light: how to make evictions deterministic and observable across restarts, how to migrate state during canary to dedicated. Candidate defaulted to engineering judgement rather than proposing explicit control-plane hooks (we should test on follow-up).
- Limited experience with production quantization impacts on eviction policy; talked about it conceptually but lacked examples of mitigation strategies (e.g., tokenization alignment causing skewed prefix distributions).

Behavioral / product fit notes:
- Communicative during pairing, asked clarifying questions rather than assuming ambiguous requirements.
- Focused on measurable SLOs (p50/p95) which aligns with our production-first ethos.
- Curious about org processes; asked several questions about Dedicated vs Private deployment constraints — suggests interest in operational tradeoffs.

Follow-ups / suggested next steps:
- Second-round: 90–120 minute systems pairing with a runtime engineer (Marcus or Aurora) to deep-dive on shard rebalancing, canary migration, and observability hooks. Include a small perf microbench exercise (Rust or Go).
- Ask candidate to bring one short example from past infra work with numbers (latency/cost before/after) — prefer a PR or benchmark artifact.
- Interviewer checklist for next round: cover state migration, deterministic eviction, monitoring instrumentation, failure recovery (crash+replay), and multi-tenant isolation.

Open questions to resolve during next session:
- How strongly do we expect candidates to propose a control-plane API for cache rollouts vs. an infra-side migration? (we should be explicit on rubrics)
- Is experience with quantization-induced skew a hard bar or a nice-to-have?

Other raw tidbits (random lines I wrote during pairing):
- Candidate said: “I optimized for fast common-case and accepted a small background reindex cost” — mirrors our continuous-batching philosophy.
- Brought up WASM as a possible isolation shim for tenant code; interesting but potentially overkill.
- Mentions prior employer had a simple nightly sweep to compact KV — low effort but large tail spikes (we should ask for metrics).

Action items (for hiring committee):
- Schedule expanded pairing + include perf harness.
- Request PR/benchmark artifact before next round.
- Recruiters: flag candidate timezones (PST) for scheduling.

Raw verdict for now: promising engineer, strong systems intuition and pragmatic tradeoffs. Not an immediate slam-dunk on ops/policy design — but advancable with targeted follow-up to validate rollout and observability skills.
